proposals.spec_says: `flush_to_ssd() -> usize` ... returns the number of memory-tier entries that have an SSD copy, or `IoError` if a write-through to SSD failed for an entry that is still in the memory tier (design invariant P9).
proposals.code_does: returns Result<usize, DispatcherError>; Ok count = resident keys for which dm.is_evictable (SSD copy AND no read/write reference), so pinned persisted entries are excluded

edits.old: `flush_to_ssd() -> usize` forces a synchronous write-through flush of pending dirty entries to SSD and returns the number of memory-tier entries that have an SSD copy, or `IoError` if a write-through to SSD failed for an entry that is still in the memory tier (design invariant P9).
edits.new: `flush_to_ssd() -> Result<usize, DispatcherError>` forces a synchronous write-through flush of pending dirty entries to SSD and returns the number of memory-tier entries that have an SSD copy, or `IoError` if a write-through to SSD failed for an entry that is still in the memory tier (design invariant P9). The count is taken after the queue has drained. It counts the resident entries that `IDispatchMap::is_evictable` reports: an SSD copy and no reference held at that moment. A persisted entry that a reader or a client `pin` holds while the count is taken is therefore not included, so the count is a lower bound. Only `Ok` versus `IoError` is the persistence guarantee.

proposals.alternative: ALIGN with A-2: add IDispatchMap::ssd_offset(key) and count ssd_offset(key).is_some(); drop the lower-bound sentence.
proposals.companion_outside_specs: components/interfaces/src/idispatcher.rs:830 doc line gets the same qualifier

proposals.spec_says: the background writer silently drops the job. The dispatch map entry remains in MemoryTier state. (Known limitation.)
proposals.code_does: job dropped without retry, caller not told, entry stays MemoryTier; failure recorded per key and flush_to_ssd returns IoError while the key is resident; cleared by a later landed write-through or when the key leaves the memory tier

edits.old: When the asynchronous background write-through fails (extent allocation failure or block device I/O error), the background writer silently drops the job. The dispatch map entry remains in MemoryTier state. (Known limitation.)
edits.new: When the asynchronous background write-through fails (extent allocation failure or block device I/O error), the background writer drops the job without retrying it, and the caller of the store is not told. The dispatch map entry remains in MemoryTier state with no SSD copy. (Known limitation.) The failure MUST be recorded per key, and `flush_to_ssd` MUST report it as `IoError` while the key is still in the memory tier (FR-056). The record is cleared when a later write-through of the key lands, or when the key is no longer in the memory tier. *(Sync 2026-10-21, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt` — code authoritative, commit `9bd231d85`, repair DIS-FLUSH-REPORTS-FAILED-WRITE. Before it the failure left no trace, so a `flush_to_ssd` followed by `clear_memory_tier` dropped the entry's only copy.)*
